note: Revision of design05.10/index.json (preserved). Interface-neutral; every assertion NOT RUN. Fixtures are referenced by frozen path and sha256; no fixture is regenerated. Prime binds the cases to the returned API.

states.judgment_recorded: reported separately; never inferred from another
states.publication_complete: reported separately; never inferred from another
states.custody_complete: reported separately; never inferred from another
states.work_complete: reported separately; never inferred from another
states.action_released: reported separately; never inferred from another

prime_interpretations.B: continue selects the review and next action; it does not release D1 by recording; resolve only the answered hold
prime_interpretations.C: freeze selected source/dependency/decision/template bytes; an unselected notes file is not automatically drift
prime_interpretations.F: unknown never becomes passed; missing required typed fields are refused; declared nullable unknowns stay explicit

cases.title: Address intake of a thin N5NN submission; preliminary judgment without custody

variations.A-base: binding builds a VALID artifact manifest in the copy: every listed file measured at setup, path base per the API's declared rule; recorded in the binding log as a binding adaptation, not as originally declared
variations.A-digest: the 05.10 manifest as frozen (VERIFICATION.md digest deliberately null) — kept separate from A-base
variations.A-missing: in the copy, delete submission.md before prepare (the Return pointer still names it)
variations.A-ambiguous: in the copy, change the Return pointer Submission line to name two different files

assertions.text: The intake index shows VERIFICATION.md, the artifact manifest and payload/parser.py as inspectable evidence, not only submission.md (C14).
The null digest is reported as a finding or missing evidence; it is not filled in, and A-base is not used to hide it (C14).
custody_complete is false. No receipt or task association is shown or written; nothing is written under a 01NN path (C16).
In a new process, read returns the recorded assessment, findings, operation and next action as supplied (C23, C28).
The supplied prose about T3 being unknown is preserved verbatim. No compute-derived summary shows T3, or the tests, as passed. Compute does not parse the prose into results (C19; 06.10 corr. 4).
work_complete and action_released are false. The review is ineligible for custody-dependent closure (C16).
The files under evidence/build05.01 are byte-identical before and after every operation (C28).

Compute derives an intake candidate identity, bound before the judgment, and a separate final review identity. The caller may echo a returned identity into a later operation; a fabricated or predicted identity is refused (C23; 06.10 corr. 2).
Both findings, F1 elevated and F2 answered, appear with their dispositions (C21).
The missing return is reported as a finding. No path is guessed; no judgment target is invented; nothing is written (C14).
The ambiguous pointer is a finding. Neither file is silently chosen (C14).

cases.title: N7NN same-pass successor after a Director hold; a manual predecessor is preserved or blocks

variations.B-tool: prerequisite: in a copy WITHOUT 06.01.review.md, record a first review through the real API with operation director-input, question Q1 and hold D1 (content from the 05.10 06.01 text). Then add 06.02.decisions.md (SYNTHETIC Director words), then record the successor (B.successor.json) for the SAME pass 05.01
variations.B-manual: the 05.10 copy as frozen: 06.01.review.md is a hand-written markdown review, not a tool record

assertions.text: The successor is recorded under the same pass's review home and its bound records. The test does not expect, and the tool does not invent, a new pass number or a new review-numbering scheme. The first tool review stays preserved and distinguishable, and the successor is explicitly selected as current (C26; 06.10 corr. 1).
The Director's words (#Q1) appear verbatim and attributed, separate from the successor's model text (C21; 06.06).

After the successor 'continue', D1 is NOT released (action_released false). Only the Q1 hold is resolved through the declared record; any other hold remains (C36; Prime interpretation, 06.10 answer B).

The hand-written 06.01.review.md is byte-identical afterwards. It is neither adopted as a tool review nor overwritten; publication either preserves it as a predecessor or is blocked or held (C26; 06.10 corr. 1).
Independent item I1 is never held (director-agreement).
Recording executes no pack, release or worker prompt (C21, C36).

cases.title: Drift after intake: selected-input change versus the tool's own pointer write versus an unselected file

variations.C-a: A-base copy; prepare and record; edit one word of the 05.01.md Scope body; publish
variations.C-b: A-base copy; prepare and record; edit the T3 row of VERIFICATION.md; publish
variations.C-c: A-base copy; prepare, record and publish normally (the tool writes its own Review-area pointer); then read and recover
variations.C-d: A-base copy; prepare and record; add a new file 06.99.notes.md (SYNTHETIC, unrelated text) on the page; publish

assertions.text: Publication is blocked or stale. The recorded judgment is unchanged; nothing is silently repinned or reapproved (C23, C28).
The same outcome for drift in selected evidence (C23).
The tool's own pointer write does not make its review stale. Publication is complete, while custody, work and release stay false or not applicable (C28; 06.10 corr. 3).
The diff of 05.01.md, before versus after, is limited to the Review - Codex Prime area. Both identities are retained (C28).
The edited bytes are left in place; the tool does not revert them.
The stale state survives a new-process read and recover (C36).

An unselected new notes file is not automatically drift; publication may proceed. (Prime interpretation, 06.10 answer C: freeze the selected inputs; reconcile only if authority or selected inputs change.)

cases.title: Judgment recorded; publication blocked by an existing manual Review-area text; new-process recovery

variations.D: A-base copy; replace 'PENDING.' in the Review - Codex Prime area with 'Manual review by hand: looks fine.' (SYNTHETIC); prepare, record, publish; end the process; new process: read, then recover

assertions.text: The manual text is byte-identical; it is not overwritten and not adopted as a review or an approval (C26).
In the new process, the exact judgment, next action and holds are returned from the tool's durable record (C23, C28).
publication_complete is false and is reported as incomplete; nothing reports completion (C28).
Removing or altering any rendered review file between processes does not change the judgment returned; the rendered file is reported as drifted or missing (C28).

cases.title: Interruption between render and pointer; a changed 'completed' output

variations.E-a: A-base copy; publish, stopping after the render and before the pointer, using a SUPPORTED stop (fault hook or process kill as the API allows); new process: status, then recover. If no supported stop exists: NOT BINDABLE
variations.E-b: A-base copy; complete a normal publish; append one line to the rendered review file; new process recover
variations.E-c: A-base copy; complete a normal publish; edit the pointer text in the Review area; new process recover

assertions.text: Before recovery, status reports publication incomplete (partial), not success (C28).

Recovery either (i) completes the pointer only after re-verifying the rendered bytes against the record, or (ii) truthfully holds with a supported next retry. Both are acceptable. Reporting complete without the verification is not. The judgment is unchanged (C28; 06.10 corr. 3).
Recovery does not report completed. It reports the rendered file as changed and does not overwrite it silently; the judgment is kept (C28 'never trusts a done label').
The same for a changed pointer area.
The source evidence files are byte-identical in every variant.

cases.title: Replay, conflict, typed-field errors, required versus nullable

variations.F-a: record A; record F.replay-same with the same operation identity
variations.F-b: record F.replay-conflict with the same identity
variations.F-c: fresh copy; pick a field the RETURNED FORM declares with a non-text type (the binding log names it) and supply a value of the wrong type
variations.F-d: fresh copy; omit a field the returned form declares REQUIRED
variations.F-e: fresh copy; supply explicit null or unknown for a field the returned form declares NULLABLE (if none exists: NOT BINDABLE)

cases.note: The 05.10 files F.wrong-type.json and F.tests-omitted.json assumed a per-test typed T3 field. They are superseded for binding (06.10 corr. 4) and preserved unchanged.

assertions.text: No duplicate authoritative result; the same stored result is returned. Diagnostic writes are allowed (C23; 06.10 corr. 4).
Refused. The authoritative record is unchanged; the conflicting input is preserved with correction help (C23).
Refused at the named declared field, naming the expected and observed type; the input is kept; nothing is recorded (C19, C23).
Refused as missing. No default is supplied (C19).
Recorded as explicit unknown or null. It never becomes passed, empty or consent (C19; Prime interpretation, 06.10 answer F).
No variant changes the source files.
